findings.title: Match statement lacks a comment explaining the new control flow
findings.body: The match statement replaces the previous `RETRYABLE_STATES` check with an explicit pattern match. While the intent is clear, the absence of a comment explaining *why* this change was made (e.g., to avoid a global constant or improve readability) makes it harder to understand the rationale behind the refactor. Add a comment summarizing the purpose of the change.
findings.suggestion:
# Explicitly match retryable states to avoid a global constant and improve clarity
    match status:

findings.title: Pattern match uses implicit wildcard instead of explicit non-retryable states
findings.body: The wildcard case `_` returns `False` for all non-retryable states, which is correct but less explicit than listing the non-retryable states (e.g., `case "success" | "pending" | _`). This could lead to confusion if new states are added later. Consider being more explicit about which states are retryable.
findings.suggestion:
case "failed" | "cancelled":
            return retries_used < retry_limit
        case "success" | "pending" | _:
            return False

summary.problem: The refactor introduces a match statement but lacks clarity in its intent and explicit handling of non-retryable states.
summary.done_well: The new control flow is concise and avoids a global constant, improving maintainability.
